SUBSTITUTE NARRATIVE (File Number: 22935-T1)
17-13-0303-C(1) Type 1 Narrative & Plans — 2343 West Chicago Avenue, Chicago, IL

Proposed Zoning:  B2-5 Neighborhood Mixed-Use District

Lot Area: 4,100.97 sq. ft.

Proposed Land Use: The Applicant is proposing to develop the subject property with a new five-
story residential building containing a lobby/condominium amenity space
at grade and six (6) dwelling units above. The first lobby/condominium
amenity space will contain approximately 600 sq. ft. of floor area. The
proposed building will measure approximately 60 ft.-8 inch. in height. The
subject property is a Transit Served Location and will be supported by six
(6) off-street parking spaces. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-0303-D optional
Administrative Adjustment and Variation and pursuant to Secs. 17-13-
1003-L and EE and 17-13-1101-B of the Chicago Zoning Ordinance, the
Applicant is seeking to increase the residential off-street parking ratio from
50% (3 parking spaces) to 100% (6 parking spaces), to reduce the rear
setback on the floors containing residential units from 30 feet to 19 ft.-4
3/16 in., (17-13-1003-L) increase the building height by 10%, and is seeking
all relief necessary, as allowed by the code, for the attached plans.

(A) | The Project’s Floor Area Ratio: 13,890 square feet (3.39 FAR)

(B) The Project’s Density (Minimum Lot Area Per D.U.): 683.50 square feet per D.U.
(6 residential units)

© The amount of off-street parking: 6 parking spaces total

*The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location based on its
proximity to Chicago Avenue CTA Buss Line. Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-EE,
the Applicant is seeking to increase the off-street parking ratio from 50% (3 parking
spaces) to 100% (6 parking spaces).

(D) _ Setbacks:

a. Front Setback: 0°
b. Side Setbacks:
East Side: 6 11/16 inches
West Side: 6 11/16 inches
c. Rear Setback: *197-4 3/16”

*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1101-B, the Applicant is seeking to reduce the rear setback
for floors containing residential units from 30 feet to 19 ft.-4 3/16 in.

(E) Building Height: *60 feet-8 inch.
*Pursuant to Sec. 17-13-1003-L, the Applicant is seeking to increase the height by

10%.

Final for Publication

Sec, 17-3-0308 Criteria for Transit-Served Locations — Supplemental Narrative Zoning Analysis

1. The subject property is a designated Transit Served Location per Sec. 17-10-0102-B
because it is located within approximately 20-25 linear feet of the Chicago Avenue CTA
Bus Line. The proposed residential building containing a lobby/condominium amenity
space at grade and six (6) residential units above will be supported by six (6) off-street
parking spaces. Pursuant to Section 17-13-1003-EE, the Applicant is seeking to permit an
increase in the residential off-street parking ratio from 50% (3 parking spaces) to 100% (6
parking spaces).

2. The Applicant complies with the requirements of Sec. 17-4-0504 for the location of the
residential building on the subject lot. The proposed location of the main building door
and entryway will be on West Chicago Avenue frontage and will have a front setback of
zero. The building’s first floor was designed with windows facing the sidewalk located
along West Chicago Avenue.

3. The Transit Friendly Development Guide defines ‘transit friendly development’ as
development which is oriented towards and integrated with adjacent transit. The proposed
residential building incorporates accessibility and connectivity to mass transit based on its
location near the Chicago CTA Bus Line. The Applicant believes the development will
improve the subject area for residents and other commuters traveling in the subject area.

4. The proposed residential building will contain approximately 600 sq. ft. of
lobby/condominium amenity space at grade and six (6) residential units above. The
proposed building will be supported by six (6) off-street parking spaces. The Applicant is
seeking administrative approval to permit the off-street parking increase for the residential
units pursuant to the TOD Ordinance.

5. The Applicant believes the proposed residential building will provide appropriate density
in the subject neighborhood. More specifically, the project will replace the existing
commercial building with a new residential building, which will provide additional
residential housing thereby meeting market demand. Based on the subject property’s
proximity to a designated Chicago Avenue CTA Bus Line, the Applicant believes the
project provides transit options and otherwise complies with the Travel Demand Study and
Management Plan rules promulgated by the Department of Transportation by serving an

area in need.
